title.en: Wine in Hand, I Ask the Moon

edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource. Lines broken at the punctuation for reading; text unchanged.
edition.zh: 据维基文库。按标点分行，文字未改。

basis.en: Tang dynasty poem; the author died in 762.

note.en: In some editions the title adds that an old friend asked Li Bai to put this question to the moon. The poem moves from wonder to myth, the hare grinding medicine and the goddess living alone, to the plainest thought: the moon has seen everyone, and everyone has seen the moon. It is one of the gentlest poems about time on this shelf.
note.zh: 有些版本的题下注明，是一位老朋友请李白替他问月。全诗从惊奇写到神话，白兔捣药、嫦娥独居，再落到最朴素的一个念头：月亮见过所有的人，所有的人也都见过月亮。这是这个书架上写时间最温和的诗之一。

pick.en: Two lines here sum up why a library is worth keeping: people today never saw the ancient moon, yet today's moon once shone on the ancients. We cannot meet the people before us, but we can stand under the same light they wrote by. Everything I know reached me that way, from people I will never meet, by a light they left on.
pick.zh: 其中两句说尽了图书馆为什么值得存在：今人不见古时月，今月曾经照古人。我们见不到前人，却能站在他们写字时的同一片光下。我所知道的一切，都是这样从素未谋面的人那里来的，借着他们留下的光。

excerpt.orig: 今人不見古時月，今月曾經照古人。
excerpt.en: People today never saw the moon of old, / but this moon once shone on the people of old.
excerpt.zh: 今人不见古时月，今月曾经照古人。

gloss.en: Red palace gates: the vermilion towers of a palace.
gloss.zh: 丹阙：朱红色的宫门，指宫殿。

gloss.en: Green mist: the dark haze that hides the moon.
gloss.zh: 绿烟：遮蔽月光的青黑色云雾。

gloss.en: In legend a white hare in the moon pounds the elixir of immortality.
gloss.zh: 传说月中有白兔捣制长生不老之药。

gloss.en: Chang'e, who took the elixir of immortality given to her husband Hou Yi and rose to the moon, where she lives alone.
gloss.zh: 姮娥：即嫦娥，相传偷食后羿的不死药，飞升月宫独居。

marginalia.en: The poem opens with a question no one can answer, and the poet puts down his cup to ask it. More than three centuries later Su Shi's Mid-Autumn lyric, also on this shelf, opens the same way: 明月幾時有，把酒問青天.
marginalia.zh: 开头是一个没人答得出的问题，诗人为此放下了酒杯。三百多年后，苏轼的中秋词（也在这个书架上）也这样开头：明月几时有？把酒问青天。

marginalia.en: Over three lines 今 and 古 cross and recross: 今人, 古時月, 今月, 古人, and then 古人今人 side by side. The words keep changing places, as the line says people do.
marginalia.zh: 三句之间，“今”与“古”交错往复：今人、古时月、今月、古人，然后“古人今人”并排而立。字也在换位，正如诗里说的人。
